title: APF Audit Event v1
description: Canonical producer-facing schema for APF common audit events. This schema validates JSON/JSONL audit records emitted by APF enforcement points. Each event type composes shared $defs blocks, so when one property inside a block is invalid the whole subschema fails and unevaluatedProperties additionally reports every field in that block as unexpected. Read the value-level violation first; the unevaluated list that accompanies it is a consequence, not a second fault.

allOf.description: Every event carries the envelope, whatever its type.

A record carrying `verdict` must not also carry the synthetic policy_verdict finding that the OpenShell wire uses to stand in for it — the same advisory signal in two shapes double-counts downstream. Producers that predate `verdict` and emit only the synthetic finding remain valid.

id.description: Reusable APF identifier string. IDs are opaque, non-empty, bounded strings intended for event, user, agent, workspace, session, policy, decision, credential, and component references.

name.description: Reusable short symbolic name for APF enum-like values, component names, profiles, resource classes, and other controlled labels.

version.description: Reusable version string. Version semantics are owned by the producing component or bundle format.

digest.description: Reusable digest string, preferably sha256:<64 hex chars>. Used for signed policy or bundle digest references.

event_type.description: APF audit event types. Each names the operation or fact being recorded — never its outcome. Authorization events carry `decision`; every other operation carries `outcome`; `reason_code` explains why. `review_request`, `review_decision` and `credential_issuance` are RESERVED: no producer emits them yet — there is no human-review gate, and no component issues credentials. They are retained so the vocabulary is stable if those capabilities ship.

decision.description: APF decision classes. `allow` and `deny` are the only members a v1 producer emits. `require_review` is RESERVED: apf-policy-eval can produce Verdict::Escalate but no review gate consumes it yet. `require_step_up`, `quarantine`, and `stop_session` are RESERVED containment actions — they answer 'what should happen to the agent' rather than 'may this request proceed', and require a substrate signalling mechanism that does not exist. Do not build consumers against the reserved values until a producer exists.

result_class.description: Normalized class for an action result, denial, timeout, partial response, or scrubbed response. `success` and `denied` are set by the typed builders; `failure`, `partial`, `timeout` and `scrubbed` are supplied by the producer on a `result` event.

reason_code.description: Stable dot-separated reason code suitable for SIEM search, tests, dashboards, and policy/debug analysis.

verb.description: Dot-separated governed action verb, scoped by the resource contract.

component.description: Metadata for the APF component or substrate wrapper that emitted the audit event.

name.description: Emitter component name, for example apf-policy-gateway or apf-openshell-middleware.

instance_id.description: Stable identity for this running component instance.

workload_identity.description: Optional workload identity used by the component to authenticate to adjacent APF components.

resource.description: Redacted resource identity and classification for a governed APF action. Do not include raw sensitive resource payloads.

type.description: Resource type, for example mailbox, repository, slack_channel, or network_destination.

id.description: Redacted or stable resource identifier appropriate for audit and SIEM search.

class.description: Resource class or provider family, for example outlook, gitlab, slack, or direct_egress.

instance.description: Optional provider-specific instance identifier, redacted if needed.

data_class.description: Data classification for the resource, for example business_email, source_code, or customer_data.

tenant.description: Optional tenant or workspace owner identifier for multi-tenant deployments.

attributes.description: Small redacted string attributes for joining and search. Sensitive field names are forbidden.

obligations.description: Obligations the enforcement point must apply. These are audit summaries of obligations, not authority expansions.

credential_scope.description: Maximum or issued credential scope associated with the decision.

redaction_profile.description: Redaction profile that must be applied before emitting audit or returning results.

max_result_size.description: Maximum result size allowed by policy obligations.

allowed_destination.description: Allowed destination identifier when the policy restricts outbound target or resource destination.

rate_limit.description: Rate limit obligation applied to the action.

audit_level.description: Required audit emission level for this action.

review_required.description: Whether the action required human review before proceeding.

credential_scope.description: Credential scope metadata proving issued credentials were bounded by policy obligations. This object must never include token material.

provider.description: Credential provider or broker, for example graph, gitlab, slack, vault, or oauth.

audience.description: Credential audience or relying party, for example graph.microsoft.com.

scopes.description: Issued or requested scopes. Values are provider scope labels, never credential values.

expires_at.description: Credential expiry timestamp. Prefer UTC RFC3339 with Z.

decision_id.description: Decision evidence identifier used to authorize this credential request.

rate_limit.description: Rate-limit obligation summary for an action.

limit.description: Maximum number of actions allowed in the window.

review_ref.description: Human-review evidence for actions that require approval before credential issuance or resource execution.

review_id.description: Identifier for the review request or decision record.

reviewer_id.description: Identifier for the human or service principal that made the review decision.

decision_at.description: Timestamp when the review decision was made. Prefer UTC RFC3339 with Z.

evidence_ref.description: Reference to review evidence, ticket, transcript, or approval artifact.

error.description: Sanitized error information for rejected policies, denied credentials, failed emissions, and failed resource calls.

message.description: Short sanitized error message safe for audit sinks. Do not include stack traces, tokens, raw payloads, or credentials.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the operation may succeed without policy or configuration changes.

delivery.description: Audit delivery metadata for sink diagnostics, local buffering, and replay accounting. RESERVED: no producer populates this yet. Retained because it describes a delivery path that exists in the sink design, not an aspiration.

sink_type.description: Audit sink type used by this delivery attempt. Only `jsonl` has an implementation; `siem` and `gateway` are RESERVED for sinks that do not exist yet.

attempt.description: Delivery attempt number for this event.

buffered.description: Whether this event was buffered locally before delivery.

replay.description: Whether this event was emitted during replay from a local buffer.

extensions.description: Deployment-specific extension object. Keys must use the x_ namespace and values must follow redacted object rules.

safe_string_map.description: Small string map for redacted attributes. Property names that commonly carry secrets or raw content are forbidden.

redacted_object.description: Object containing only redacted, bounded audit-safe summary values. It must not contain raw user content, secrets, credentials, or sensitive payloads.

redacted_value.description: Recursive redacted value allowed in audit summaries and extensions. Strings are bounded; object keys that commonly carry secrets or raw content are forbidden.

finding.description: One observation emitted alongside a decision by the policy engine's effect stage. Findings do not change the decision; they record what was detected.

kind.description: Finding category, from the PolicyFinding `type` field, e.g. secret_detected. Human-authored descriptive text: bounded in length but otherwise unconstrained, because rejecting a label must never cost the audit record that carries it.

label.description: Specific label within the category. Static, or resolved at evaluation time from a `label_source` annotation, e.g. github_pat or "AWS access key". Deliberately unpatterned: this value is produced at runtime from annotation data with no charset guarantee, and a charset rule here would reject the whole event rather than just the label.

confidence.description: Detector confidence in percent, when the annotator supplies one.

verdict.description: Advisory signal accompanying a decision, from apf_policy_eval::Verdict. Orthogonal to `decision`: `warn` is an allow with elevated signal, `escalate` asks for review. Without this field a warn is indistinguishable from a plain allow.

envelope.description: Fields every APF audit event carries, whatever its type.

schema_version.description: APF audit schema version. The emitter sets this to identify the canonical event contract used by this record.

event_id.description: Unique identifier for this single audit event. Generated by the emitter and never reused.

timestamp.description: UTC RFC3339 timestamp generated by the emitting component.

event_type.description: Machine-readable event category that determines which event-specific fields are required.

correlation_id.description: Identifier shared across all audit events for one governed action or workflow step.

enforcement_point_id.description: Identifier for the emitting enforcement point or APF component.

runtime_substrate.description: Runtime substrate identifier, for example openshell.

component.description: Emitter component metadata: component name, version, instance identity, and optional workload identity.

causation_id.description: Event or operation ID that caused this event.

trace_id.description: Optional trace identifier for OpenTelemetry or APF trace context.

span_id.description: Optional span identifier for OpenTelemetry or APF trace context.

device_id.description: Optional device or host identity from trusted runtime context. Use when the deployment can distinguish device from workspace.

deployment_profile.description: Deployment profile bound to the active policy and runtime context, for example dev, enterprise, or safety profile.

reason.description: Short sanitized human-readable explanation for the decision, result, rejection, or denial. Do not include raw payloads, stack traces, secrets, or credential material.

delivery.description: Optional audit delivery metadata for local buffering, replay, or sink diagnostics.

extensions.description: Allowlisted extension namespace for deployment-specific redacted metadata. Extension keys must start with x_.

subject_identity.description: Who the action was taken for. Absent on events that precede any session.

user_id.description: Human or delegating principal from trusted runtime context.

agent_id.description: Agent, persona, or workload identity from trusted runtime context.

workspace_id.description: Stable identifier for the runtime environment or workspace where the agent action occurred, as named by the substrate. Source of truth is trusted runtime context, not agent-supplied input.

session_id.description: Identifier for the specific agent/runtime session within the workspace. Used to join APF events with substrate events and bypass-denial evidence.

policy_identity.description: Which signed policy was in force. bundle_digest is the identity; policy_revision is the ordering signal.

bundle_digest.description: Digest of the active signed policy bundle.

bundle_id.description: Identifier of the APF signed bundle that supplied the active policy, from verified bundle state.

policy_revision.description: Monotonic policy revision (PolicyBundle policy_revision) of the bundle in force. Ordering and anti-rollback signal; identity is carried by bundle_digest. Absent when the bundle could not be parsed, since an unparsed bundle has no readable revision.

signer_id.description: Identifier of the signer that produced the active bundle signature, from verified bundle state.

trust_root_id.description: Identifier of the trust root used to verify the active bundle.

decision_fields.description: The shape of a governed authorization decision.

resource.description: Redacted resource identifier and classification for the governed action.

verb.description: Governed APF action verb, for example mail.search, repo.write, or slack.post.

decision.description: Decision class that governed this action or downstream event.

decision_id.description: Identifier for decision evidence, used downstream to prove an enforcement point acted on a valid decision.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable reason for the decision, result, rejection, or denial.

argument_summary.description: Redacted request argument summary. Do not place raw user content or secrets here.

obligations.description: Structured obligations returned by policy evaluation and applied by the enforcement point.

result_class.description: Normalized result class for the action outcome.

result_summary.description: Redacted result summary. Do not place raw response content or secrets here.

review_decision_event.description: RESERVED — no producer. The outcome of a human review requested by review_request. Carries `decision` because it records a decision.

review_ref.description: Human-review evidence reference and status for review-required actions.

resource.description: Redacted resource identifier and classification for the governed action.

verb.description: Governed APF action verb, for example mail.search, repo.write, or slack.post.

decision.description: Decision class that governed this action or downstream event.

decision_id.description: Identifier for decision evidence, used downstream to prove an enforcement point acted on a valid decision.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable reason for the decision, result, rejection, or denial.

advisory_signals.description: Observations and the advisory verdict the policy engine emitted alongside a decision. Only the event types produced by an evaluation carry these — credential and review events are downstream of a decision and do not re-report its signals.

findings.description: Observations emitted alongside the decision, on allows and denies alike. Order is significant and mirrors bundle manifest order, then policy order within each rule. Not deduplicated: the effect engine pushes one entry per firing rule, so two rules reporting the same detection legitimately produce identical entries. maxItems matches the middleware's MAX_FINDINGS_PER_STAGE.

verdict.description: Advisory verdict accompanying the decision. Producers set this from the evaluator's Verdict and must NOT additionally emit a synthetic warn/escalate finding — that duplication exists only on the OpenShell wire, which has findings but no verdict field.

header_mutation_record.description: One applied header mutation. Records the header NAME and the action, never the value — an injected credential is exactly what would be in the value.

name.description: Header name, e.g. authorization. Bounded but unpatterned: RFC 7230 token syntax permits !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~, which the middleware's own validator accepts, so a charset rule would reject the record over a legal header name.

patch_record.description: One applied body patch. Records the target PATH and the operation, never the value — a patch value is the sensitive content the redaction exists to remove.

path.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, e.g. /messages/0/content. Bounded but otherwise unconstrained: pointer segments can contain arbitrary object keys, and a charset rule here would reject the whole audit event over a path.

op.description: Mirrors `apf_policy_eval::PatchOp`. A path that was `replace`d was redacted in altered form; a path that was `remove`d is gone entirely — materially different answers to what the request looked like when it left.

effects.description: What the enforcement point applied to the request in flight. Distinct from `obligations`, which records what policy REQUIRED: merged, an unapplied obligation would be indistinguishable from an applied one. Records paths and names only — a patch value is the sensitive content the redaction exists to remove. Absent means unmodified, so the object must assert at least one real mutation: `{}`, `{"patch_count": 0}` and `{"payload_replaced": false}` are all rejected.

patch_count.description: RFC 6902 operations applied to the request body. Authoritative: the engine applies patches with no cap, so `patches` is truncated to 64 while this count stays exact. `patch_count` greater than `patches` length means the list was truncated, not that the schema disagreed.

patches.description: The patches applied, truncated to 64 — `patch_count` is authoritative for the total. This is what answers 'was the secret field redacted, or a different one?' — a count alone cannot.

payload_replaced.description: The body was replaced wholesale rather than patched. Takes precedence over patches in the engine, so both counts may be zero when this is true.

header_mutations.description: Bounded at 64 to match the middleware's own MAX_HEADER_MUTATIONS, which hard-denies above that — so no producer-legal request can overflow this.

applied_effects.description: Effects applied by an enforcement point that rewrites requests in flight.

effects.description: What was applied to the request. Absent when nothing was changed.

caller_kind.description: Class of caller that presented the credential, as named by the runtime substrate — for example gateway or supervisor under OpenShell. Open rather than enumerated: caller classes are defined by the substrate's own authentication protocol, and a closed list would reject an auth denial from any other runtime outright.

outcome.description: Result of an operation event. `success` — the operation completed. `refused` — a deliberate rejection by policy, integrity, or governance checks. `failure` — an operational error (I/O, signing, persistence), not a judgement. Authorization events do not use this field; they carry `decision` instead.

operation_fields.description: The shape of an operation event: what was operated on, and how it came out. `outcome` is required on every operation event; `decision` is not permitted — that field belongs to authorization.

error.description: Detail for a refused or failed outcome.

resource.description: Redacted resource identifier and classification for the governed action.

verb.description: Governed APF action verb, for example mail.search, repo.write, or slack.post.

validation_checks.description: Which integrity checks a validation actually ran. A check that could not run (e.g. no spec digest was present to compare) is listed as skipped rather than silently counted as passed — a validation that skipped a check proves less than one that performed it.

performed.description: Checks that ran, in execution order.

skipped.description: Checks that could not run, with the reason in reason_code.

authorization_event.description: An authorization decision on a governed action — the only event type that carries `decision`. Covers allows and denials alike, from the PDP and from the egress middleware; a denial's policy explanation rides in `error` or `reason`. Records the middleware *instructing* a refusal or mutation, not independent confirmation that the substrate applied it.

error.description: The policy's own explanation of a denial.

authentication_event.description: A rejection at the authentication / caller-access boundary. Not only 'identity could not be verified': also a correctly-authenticated caller that lacks permission for the RPC or the sandbox. No policy was consulted, so no policy identity is carried.

allOf.description: Sandbox binding is an OpenShell concept: a binding exists only for the supervisor caller class, since every other class authenticates without one. Substrates that scope credentials differently should record their equivalent in `extensions` rather than reusing these fields.

result_class.description: An authentication event records that the caller was REFUSED; any other result class contradicts the event type.

caller_kind.description: The caller class established by authentication, when one was established. Present for a caller that authenticated but was refused; absent when authentication itself failed.

resource.description: The resource the refused call targeted, when known. Optional: a credential failure is rejected before the request body is parsed.

verb.description: The action the refused call attempted, when known. Optional for the same reason as `resource`.

caller_sandbox_id.description: The sandbox the presented credential is bound to, from the verified token. OpenShell-specific. Unpatterned: the sandbox id is opaque to APF.

claimed_sandbox_id.description: The sandbox the refused request claimed to act on, from the request context. With `caller_sandbox_id` this answers which sandbox impersonated which. Unpatterned: this value is attacker-controlled, and a charset rule would drop the record of the impersonation attempt it exists to capture.

outcome.description: Authentication events record refusals only: a successful auth is not audited as a standalone event.

policy_verification_event.description: A signed bundle was checked — signature, manifest hashes, expiry, runtime compatibility, counter regression. Verification success does not establish activation; that is a separate policy_activation event.

rejection_reasons.description: Every check that failed, as normalized codes. verify_bundle accumulates rather than short-circuits — a bundle can fail expiry and runtime-compat and the counter at once — so `reason_code` names the primary cause and this lists the full set. Human-readable detail belongs in error.message.

policy_activation_event.description: A verified bundle was put into (or removed from) force: initial load, hot-swap, or a refused activation (counter regression, persist failure, compile failure). The digest names exactly which policy is now enforcing.

policy_distribution_event.description: A policy document was requested from a serving surface: vended, refused (unknown document, invalid request), or served degraded. Carries no consumer identity — it records that a document was served, not to whom; suppression of unchanged re-serves means absence of a record is not absence of a fetch.

policy_refresh_event.description: An operator asked the service to reload policy. Records the request; the resulting load is its own policy_verification/policy_activation pair.

provenance_signing_event.description: Minting the provenance token that accompanies a vended document. A failure here does NOT stop the document being served — it is served unsigned, and this record is the only evidence of that degradation.

served_unsigned.description: True when the document was served despite the signing failure.

policy_injection_event.description: Policy material was injected into a resource specification at admission (MODIFY_OPERATION): patches prepared and provenance stamped. Records what the injection changed — it does not prove the runtime applied it; that is what admission_validation later checks.

admission_validation_event.description: The admission-time integrity check (VALIDATE): is the specification still the one policy injection produced? `checks` records which comparisons actually ran — a validation that skipped a check proves less than one that performed it.

config_governance_event.description: A governance decision over configuration-changing operations: approval-mode changes, direct policy mutation, deletion attempts. Refusals here are governance, not authentication — the caller is who it claims to be.

review_request_event.description: RESERVED — no producer. A decision was deferred to human review; records the request for review, not its outcome.

review_ref.description: Human-review evidence reference and status for review-required actions.

resource.description: Redacted resource identifier and classification for the governed action.

verb.description: Governed APF action verb, for example mail.search, repo.write, or slack.post.

decision_id.description: Identifier for decision evidence, used downstream to prove an enforcement point acted on a valid decision.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable reason for the decision, result, rejection, or denial.

credential_issuance_event.description: RESERVED — no producer. A credential was requested for a governed action: issued (`outcome: success`, with scope and result class) or refused (`outcome: refused`, with error detail).

credential_request_id.description: Identifier for the request associated with credential issuance or denial.

credential_scope.description: Credential provider, audience, scopes, and TTL issued or requested. Must never include credential material.

result_class.description: Only a successful issuance has a credential to classify; pinned to success and forbidden unless outcome is success. Read outcome for success vs refused.

error.description: Sanitized error metadata. Must not contain stack traces, secrets, raw payloads, or credential material.

resource.description: Redacted resource identifier and classification for the governed action.

verb.description: Governed APF action verb, for example mail.search, repo.write, or slack.post.

decision_id.description: Identifier for decision evidence, used downstream to prove an enforcement point acted on a valid decision.

security_state.description: Resolved security state of the service's startup configuration. `secure` means every configured control is active; `degraded` means at least one control is deliberately or accidentally weakened while the process continues to serve; `rejected` means preflight refused to start.

policy_service_startup_event.description: The security state of the configuration the policy service started with. Emitted once per boot, healthy or not. Carries no policy identity and no subject: it precedes both.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable reason for the decision, result, rejection, or denial.

error.description: Sanitized error metadata. Must not contain stack traces, secrets, raw payloads, or credential material.

rejection_reasons.description: Every check that failed, as normalized codes. verify_bundle accumulates rather than short-circuits — a bundle can fail expiry and runtime-compat and the counter at once — so `reason_code` names the primary cause and this lists the full set. Human-readable detail belongs in error.message.

security_state.description: Resolved security state of the startup configuration. Present on policy_service_startup events, which are emitted once per startup.
